sections.what_happened: With 25.2% of ballot boxes counted as of 04:05 Israel time, CEC partial results give the pro-Netanyahu bloc 63 seats and the anti-Netanyahu bloc 49, with the nonaligned Joint List holding the remaining 8. Parties below the 3.25% threshold in this partial: Ra'am 3.2%, Reservists 2.9%, People of Israel 1.8%, Charedi Public 0.2%. The results are partial and will change; double-envelope ballots (soldiers etc.) are counted later. This is a MATERIAL move from the 0600 scan's 18.8%/20.1% snapshot (Netanyahu bloc 63, opposition 49, Arab 7 in that table) and from the exit polls (Netanyahu bloc 50, opposition 52, Arab parties 17-18): the counted partial now favours the Netanyahu bloc, and the Arab-party total in the partial (8) is far below the exit-poll 17-18. At Likud election HQ, Netanyahu said Israel has a 'historic, one-time opportunity' to defeat Iran 'once and for all' and called it a 'shame' that parties are willing to cooperate with Arab parties; he also claimed a 'decisive majority' among the Zionist public and plans a right-wing government, while refraining from declaring victory. TRACKER-ONLY NOTE (do NOT headline): The Petek tracker page, crawled 06:58 , shows a further advance to 32.56% counted at 04:51 Israel time (06:51 ) with the Netanyahu bloc at 58, Change bloc 47, Arab parties 15, Ra'am clearing the threshold at 3.67%. Petek holds NO declared tier in the source registry and this later figure has no second-family corroboration in-window, so it is recorded here as a tracker reading only, NOT as the verified count figure.
sections.what_verified: Count figures: primary-source single family -- the CEC itself (T1 official/primary data). Times of Israel (T3) is the carrier of the same CEC data, not an independent corroboration of it, so it is NOT counted as a second family. Gate: primary_source_single_family=true for the count figures, as in the 0600 record. Exit-poll baseline: Reuters T1 + Channels 11/12/13 via Times of Israel T3 (prior scans). Petek tracker: NO declared tier, excluded from corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: The partial is NOT a projection: early-reporting areas skew the picture (prior scans), and the Petek tracker-only reading at 32.56% already moves the blocs (58-47-15) away from the 25.2% split, proving the partial moves fast. Ra'am sat below threshold in the 18.8% table (2.76%) and at 3.2% here, but clears it (3.67%) in the uncorroborated Petek reading -- threshold survival is genuinely undecided. Netanyahu's 'decisive majority' claim contradicts the exit polls (bloc 50) and rests on the partial, not a final result. Eisenkot's victory claim and Lapid's 'crushing defeat' line (0100 scan) cut the other way and are both pre-count rhetoric.
sections.why_matters: The count flips the script: exit polls said Netanyahu 50, the real ballots so far say 63 -- but a quarter of the vote is not a result, and the Arab parties' kingmaker crown is hanging on 0.05 points of threshold.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW UPDATE to totw-20261028-0000-09/0100-01/0200-01/0300-01/0400-01/0500-01/0600-01 (Israel election night) -- CEC real count reaches 25.2% of ballot boxes; Netanyahu bloc 63, opposition 49, Joint List 8 in the partial; Ra'am below threshold at 3.2%; Netanyahu claims 'historic, one-time opportunity' on Iran

totw_analysis: Our read: The count flips the script: exit polls said Netanyahu 50, the real ballots so far say 63 -- but a quarter of the vote is not a result, and the Arab parties' kingmaker crown is hanging on 0.05 points of threshold. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Exit polls vs real ballots: did the polls miss a Netanyahu-bloc surge, or do the first-counted areas just skew right -- and will the Arab parties, crowned kingmakers by the exit polls, survive the threshold in the real count?
